newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended a dull day lower on Tuesday, as key U.S. economic data failed to inspire trade amid scarce domestic news.
The market continued to follow fellow markets given the lack of clear trading incentives.

"The truth is there is nothing special to comment on," an analyst said. "The only thing we were waiting for were the indicators coming from the U.S. and these also didn't move the market because they came out close to expectations." The U.S. second-quarter employment cost index rose 0.8 percent as forecast.
July U.S. consumer confidence also slipped to 126.5 percent from June's 129.9 percent and against forecasts for a climb to 130.4 percent. But that data had little impact on markets.

Dealers said there was little to get the market going in the short-term, and the yield spread to the German 10-year benchmark was likely to continue to trade near 60 basis points. It ended Tuesday at 62 basis points.
"The question is fairly simple. We are dedicated to watching the spread with Germany, and the market is trying not to let it move very much from 60 basis points," an analyst said.
For now, any major market-moving data are seen coming from abroad.
"There is confidence in the domestic economy, and the market is paying more attention to what is happening abroad, above all, to the numbers from the U.S.," another analyst said.
